To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
K(+) uptake in barley leaves is driven by voltage-gated K(+) channels and by non-selective cation channels.

1) K(+) accumulation rates in barley leaf cells are not limited by K(+)-selectivity or voltage-dependence of channels; and 2) under saline conditions, downregulation of voltage-independent K(+)-channels may reduce the capacity of leaf cells for K(+) accumulation.
the K(+)-selectivity of the Na(+)-permeable current in the emerging leaf zone is lost under salinity conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrophysiological characterization and the functional role of ion channels involved in the uptake of K(+) into leaf cells of barley.
the characterization of ion currents involved in K(+) accumulation into growing and non-growth leaf cells.
the question how plants are able to maintain their growth under saline conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the capacity of K(+) uptake by the cell membrane is high enough to meet the requirements of growth and that the capacity of the cell membrane for K(+) influx is sufficient for growth under saline conditions.
the capacity for growth-associated K(+) uptake in barley leaf cells is limited by the rate of K(+) supply from the apoplast.
ion channels do not limit growth related K(+) uptake in growing barley leaf epidermal cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of K(+) accumulation into growing cells is not determined by the properties of K(+) channels.
K(+) uptake is a complex phenomenon that involves a variety of transporters, and that the contribution of individual pathways to K(+) accumulation varies with tissue and environmental conditions.
the K(+) uptake in the growing barley leaf is mediated by voltage-dependent and voltage-independent K(+) channels, but the contribution of voltage-independent K(++) channels is small.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ion channels play an important role in K(+) accumulation, and that the role of channels may vary between growing and non-growing tissue.
ion channels play an important role in K+ uptake into growing and emerged blade zone leaf cells.
ion channels are important in determining the rates of K(?) uptake and accumulation by growing cells.
